name: Shethar-Boznai
title: Persian Governor's Envoy
summary: Shethar-Boznai was a Persian official who served under the governor Tattenai in the province Beyond the River (west of the Euphrates). He was involved in investigating and questioning the Jews' rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem after the exile, and sent a letter to King Darius to confirm whether the Jews had permission to build.

keyEvents.title: Investigation of Temple Construction
keyEvents.description: Shethar-Boznai came with Tattenai to Jerusalem to investigate who had given the Jews permission to rebuild the temple and restore the walls.

keyEvents.title: Interrogation of Jewish Elders
keyEvents.description: Shethar-Boznai and Tattenai asked the Jewish elders for the names of those leading the construction work, and the Jews replied that they were acting on God's command and with permission from King Cyrus.

keyEvents.title: Letter to King Darius
keyEvents.description: Shethar-Boznai was a co-sender of the letter sent to King Darius in Persia, where they reported on the construction work in Jerusalem and asked the king to search the archives to find out whether Cyrus had truly given permission.

keyEvents.title: God's eye over the Jewish elders
keyEvents.description: While the letter was on its way to Darius, Shethar-Bozenai and Tattenai allowed the Jews to continue the work because God's eye watched over the Jewish elders.

keyEvents.title: Received King Darius's response
keyEvents.description: King Darius found Cyrus's original decree and ordered Shethar-Bozenai and Tattenai to stay away from Jerusalem, let the Jews complete the temple construction, and support them with funds from the treasury.

keyEvents.title: Obedience to the king's command
keyEvents.description: Shethar-Bozenai and Tattenai obeyed King Darius's command and allowed the Jews to continue building without hindrance, which contributed to the completion of the temple.
